(i) the GDS and network analyses are useful tools to investigate genetic structure and diversity in clonal organisms, (ii) in the marine plant P. oceanica the genetic structure of populations is shaped by the combined action of outcrossing, somatic mutations and clonal growth, and (iii) networks based on genetic distance among genets are characterized by a ‘small-world’, with high degree of connectivity and a high level of substructure, suggesting that the genetic structure is not homogeneous

(1) the genetic structure of P. oceanica is shaped by a combination of outcrossing, clonal growth, and somatic mutations; (2) the genetic structure is organized in subfamilies, which may be related to the presence of subpopulations within the population; and (3) the genetic structure shows a ‘small-world topology’, which may be related with the high degree of connectivity observed in the population.

clonal growth and out-crossing are apparently dominant, whereas selfing, somatic mutations and immigration appear to play only a marginal role in shaping the genetic diversity in the clonal organism studied.
